rows.evidence: Q1: Sections III-VI, Tables 1-4 - the author compiles state-level data for 14 Indian states at four time points and runs his own correlation and regression analyses of irrigated area per thousand rural population against rural poverty and related variables.
rows.notes: The study is about the relationship between total irrigated area (all methods) and rural poverty across Indian states. It contains no data on drip or micro-irrigation, water consumption, or energy/electricity use. The claim about micro-irrigation consuming less water and energy is not addressed at all; the review may have intended a different Narayanamoorthy 2001 paper on drip irrigation.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections III-VI, Tables 1-4 - own regression/correlation analysis of state-level irrigation and poverty data for 14 states at four time points.
rows.notes: The study reports positive regressions of foodgrain productivity (PFG) and foodgrain production per head on irrigated area per thousand rural population (Table 1), but this concerns irrigation in general, not drip or micro-irrigation. No drip yield data are reported.

notes: Full text appears complete. The document is a statewise econometric analysis of irrigated area (all irrigation types) versus rural poverty in India, 1972-73 to 1987-88. It makes no mention of drip, sprinkler or micro-irrigation, water saving, energy, weeds or soil erosion, so none of the four claims is supported; the review probably intended a different Narayanamoorthy 2001 publication on drip irrigation economics.
